method.positive_lag: Compare input(t) to output(t+lag): positive means output is late.
method.interpolation: None: integer sample lags avoid attenuating the noisy policy endpoint.
method.endpoint_time: Accepted, clipped policy endpoint is dated at policy_segment_times[-1], i.e. trace time after the10ms step; decision was made10ms earlier.
method.decision_time_convention: If endpoint is dated at decision time, its lag relative to target decreases10ms (more apparent anticipation) and endpoint-to-served lag increases10ms; target-to-served lag is unchanged.
method.local_windows: Each complete target-phase cycle; bounds are sampled phase wraps.
method.reward_counterfactual: Frozen-trace rescoring only; q and qdot shifted jointly per joint. No altered physics or successful-contact claim.

limitations: A lag is a descriptive best shift, not a pure fixed transport delay or causal fraction of the physical error.
Raw endpoint is oscillatory; low endpoint-to-served correlation makes its single lag weak evidence.
No slew in these traces. Endpoint after action clipping equals accepted endpoint; the within-step raw PCHIP reference runs from the served anchor to this endpoint.
Reported precision is10ms; lowpass delay is frequency-dependent, with nonlinear jerk limiting.
One deterministic episode per checkpoint. Historical best87 is more mature and has a different target.
Offline reward rescore does not recalculate contact, dynamics, phase events or penalties and cannot predict rollout return.
